correctness.rationale: For generic complex symmetric sparse matrix on a spider T, differentiation in independent diagonal variables makes Sing(det M=0) exactly corank>=2. Path blocks with all nonzero edge parameters have nullity <=1, and if s singular arms attach at center, global nullity=s-1, yielding Z_{ijk} for triples. If some edge parameter vanishes, cut-forest ranks put the point either in Y_e (singular components on opposite sides) or in a centered truncated spider with three singular arms, again Z. Irreducibility follows from leaf expansion and primitive linear-polynomial Gauss; Y_e and Z_{ijk} have disjoint-variable prime complete-intersection defining equations. Their codim3 degrees are |A_e||B_e| and ell_i ell_j ell_k; rank-three restriction to Sym² of the two-dimensional kernel yields generic transverse uv-w² ordinary nodes, and Serre R1/S2 yields normality. Independently checked aggregate degree identity for 5,440 arm-length profiles; source script inspected, its claimed finite ranks are not universal proof.
